Use case: ads-marketing.
Create ONE photorealistic first-frame still for a deliberately low-budget Korean absurdist comedy commercial. Widescreen true 16:9, no letterboxing, no collage. Not a polished corporate advertising portrait. Cheap practical props, earnest exaggerated sports ceremony, slightly flat tiny-gym lighting except bright light on commentator.
Location: small makeshift sports broadcast set in an ordinary empty cream-wall school gym, blue tape marks on parquet floor. Left grey folding table and grey folding chair; center-right very LOW broad square wheeled podium, its top only 15 cm from floor including conspicuous casters. A practical black push bar rises from the back of the podium. No text or numbers on anything.
Exactly three fictional Korean adults, no crowd.
P: woman in her 30s, short black ponytail, cobalt blue tracksuit jacket with ONE white stripe and matching blue trousers, white sneakers. She stands on the low podium, holds a SMALL BLACK HANDHELD MICROPHONE just below her chin, lips about to open, determined calm expression.
T: man in his 30s with short black hair, yellow tracksuit jacket, black trousers. He stands to P's right. In ONE hand he holds a YELLOW PAPER CUP containing large colored paper confetti at shoulder height, poised but he has NOT thrown any; his other hand relaxed. No airborne confetti.
R: male commentator in his 40s, neat side part, cream blazer, RED BOW TIE, white shirt, black trousers. He sits at the LEFT folding table leaning forward with exaggerated anticipatory delight. On table ONLY a red headset, no microphone, books or papers.
Beside T on a low prop stand stand a large lightweight GOLD FOIL PAPER TROPHY (70cm tall, wide cup with two loop handles, round unmarked base) and ONE bunch of red flowers in white wrapping. No trophy in P's hands.
Camera medium wide/full body, front 3/4 enough to clearly see 15cm podium, P's feet, all three actors and trophy shape. Single moment BEFORE first confetti throw, faces unobstructed. Keep hands and separate objects physically clear. No captions, words, event title, logos, brands, medals, notebook or watermark.
